headline: Best third-quarter revenue in a decade, returns improve
summary_short: Citigroup earned $5.2B ($2.85 per diluted share, +53% y/y) on revenue of $23.8B, up 8% y/y, as Services, Wealth, Markets and Banking all grew and expenses fell 2%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8% y/y on Services (+15%), Wealth (+15%), Markets (+6%) and Banking (+6%), with net interest income up 14%. Operating expenses fell 2% as the prior-year Banamex goodwill impairment dropped out. The provision rose to $2.6B on a $369M net reserve build tied to the macro outlook and portfolio growth. Loans grew 12% and deposits 9% y/y. CET1 held at 12.8%, RoTCE was 11.5%, and Citi returned $4.1B to common shareholders. Management said it expects to exceed this year's return target.
confidence_notes: Prior-year EPS of $1.86 and net income of $3.8B include a $714M after-tax Banamex goodwill impairment; excluding it, EPS rose 27% (prior-year $2.24). The resolver's shard EPS ($2.83) is Yahoo-sourced; the release's diluted $2.85 is used here. Net income is Citigroup's net income after non-controlling interests. No numeric forward guidance was stated; the release says only that Citi expects to exceed this year's return target.

drivers.explanation: Growth in Services, Wealth, Markets and Banking, partly offset by a decline in All Other; net interest income rose 14% while non-interest revenue fell 4%.

Absence of the prior-year goodwill impairment and lower professional services costs, partly offset by higher transactional, deposit insurance and compensation expenses; excluding the notable item, expenses rose 3%.
Higher revenues and lower expenses, partially offset by a higher provision for credit losses.
Higher net income and a lower share count from repurchases.
Net credit losses were $2.2B and a net reserve build of $369M, driven by changes in the macroeconomic outlook and portfolio growth.
Net income and lower DTA deductions were offset by buybacks, dividends and unrealized losses on AFS securities.
CEO Jane Fraser cited the best third-quarter revenue in a decade, positive operating leverage and meaningful return improvement, with Services up 15% and over $4B returned to shareholders.
